newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait govt panel support BAe missile preference.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait govt panel support BAe missile preference.

text.p: The Kuwaiti government told parliament on Monday that a specialised panel had recommended purchasing British Aerospace Plc Sea Skua missiles for a naval contract.

Parliament's protection of public funds committee, which has repeatedly questioned the government's Sea Skua decision, quoted acting prime minister and foreign minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah as telling the committee that no deal had been signed.
A statement by the committee said Sheikh Sabah had informed it at a meeting on Monday that a defence ministry panel had picked the Sea Skua over France's Aerospatiale MM-15.

The statement did not give a value for the deal, but industry experts had earlier told Reuters the total Sea Skua package could be worth up to $150 million. Kuwaiti papers had earlier valued the deal at $90 million.
The government had previously said its decision to buy the Sea Skua was final but it decided to form the defence ministry panel in response to strong criticism from parliament.

Kuwait told Britain more than a year ago that it would buy British surface-to-surface missiles, but the deal has faced problems in parliament, which questioned why a cheaper offer by France for Aerospatiale missiles was dropped.
The defence ministry panel is the third to review the deal. The first picked the French missiles but the second chose the Sea Skua. The members of the latest panel did not serve on the previous two.

The public funds committee "clarified that if the government proceeds to take a decision in favour of the British deal then it (the government) is politically responsible and the committee has no choice but to deal with this fact...

"But if the decision has not yet been taken the committee urges the government to listen to the views of the members of the first (defence ministry) panel who unanimously objected to go ahead with the British missiles."
Monday's committee meeting was attended by several ministers, senior military officers and top accounting officials.
Kuwait wants the missiles to arm eight fast patrol boats ordered from France in 1995 in a contract worth $500 million.
